text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Erbakan accuses the West of supporting separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels and praises Libyan president Muammer Gaddafi, despite Gaddafi's open support for the PKK during Erbakan's visit to Libya.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller listens nervously to Erbakan on his return from a controversial African trip.
- Turkish troops kill 191 Kurdish rebels in separate clashes in the last four days.
- Erbakan defends his visit to Libya and says he will silence the strong criticism of the tour.
- Foreign Minister Ciller makes an unexpected visit to military chiefs, seen as the guardians of the state's strict secularism, as tension mounts between secularists and Islamists.
- President Suleyman Demirel says there is no Kurdish minority in Turkey during his visit to Rome.
- State Minister Ayfer Yilmaz says expectations for exports because of the customs union with the European Union have not been realised.
- The Turkish budget for 1997 is to be studied by the International Monetary Fund delegation coming to Turkey on Oct 14.
- A Turkish F-16 warplane crashes near Chios Island in the Aegean as Greek planes violate Turkish airspace.
